subject: Throughput sizing post-call: latency & peak QPS follow-ups
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finexanalytics.com>; Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@finexanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing post-call: latency & peak QPS follow-ups

Hi Amelia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + a few follow-ups to make sure our sizing recommendation matches your workload:

Summary:
- Primary use: customer-facing chat assistant (streaming) + async batch reranking for daily reports.
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 350ms token response (interactive streaming experience).
- Expected steady-state: ~120 concurrent active users during business hours, average session length 6 turns (~450 tokens per session).
- Peak events: product launch spikes up to 800 concurrent users over ~10 minutes, roughly 4x steady-state QPS for ~30 minutes.

Requests for next steps (can you confirm the items below?):
1) Streaming requirements: are you doing token-level streaming to web clients? If so, typical chunk size and client-side buffering?
2) Concurrency vs per-user QPS: do you expect many short sessions (high QPS per user) or fewer long sessions?
3) Payloads: please share a couple sample requests (anonymized) — especially the long prompts and few-shot examples.
4) SLO tolerances for fallbacks: if we need to route to a lower-cost model under load, what's acceptable quality drop / retry behavior?

I attached the SLO worksheet template if useful. I can run an initial sizing based on the numbers above once we get the sample payloads and confirm streaming chunking.

Next steps: if you can drop the sample payloads and confirm streaming chunk size, I'll run two sizing options (optimal-latency and cost-optimized) and share recommended capacity (GPU pool estimate + expected tokens/sec and QPS) by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com

---
Attachment: finex_slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet with SLO fields)

From: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finexanalytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@finexanalytics.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing post-call: latency & peak QPS follow-ups

Thanks Rafael — good write-up. Quick answers below and attaching sample payloads.

1) Streaming: yes, we stream token-by-token to the browser. Chunking is 1 token per event, but client-side aggregates to ~50ms update windows.
2) Concurrency: mix — typical is many short sessions (QPS-heavy) for support chat, but the advisor flow has longer sessions. For sizing please assume 60% of traffic is short QPS-style, 40% long sessions.
3) Payloads: attached finex_sample_payloads.json with representative prompts (anonymized).
4) Fallback tolerances: for spikes we can accept routing to a smaller model with a 7-10% reduction in accuracy for up to 15 minutes; beyond that we prefer throttling vs degraded quality.

Other notes: peak patterns usually align with marketing emails and end-of-quarter reporting — we saw a 3.8x spike last quarter for ~25 minutes.

Let us know if you need additional telemetry (p95 token latency observed today from our current provider).

Best,
Amelia Johnson
Head of Product — AI Experiences
FinEx Analytics
amelia.johnson@finexanalytics.com

---
Attachment: finex_sample_payloads.json

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finexanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing post-call: latency & peak QPS follow-ups

Appreciate the payloads — reviewing now. A couple clarifying questions after a quick pass:

- Tokenization: are the payloads pre-tokenized on your side or raw text? We need to estimate tokens/sec.
- Streaming chunk size: since client aggregates to 50ms windows, for sizing we should plan for bursty small writes; is that acceptable?
- Peak concurrency distribution: for the 800 concurrent peak, is that concentrated in a single region/zone? Any geo-split?

Tentative plan: I'll run two sims — (1) low-latency config (dedicated pool, FP16 with aggressive batching tuned for streaming) to hit p95 <= 350ms; (2) cost-optimized config (quantized model + larger batching) with p95 ~500-600ms but lower cost per token.

I'll include tokens/sec, QPS, and estimated GPUs (dedicated instances + headroom for autoscale) in the report. Expect that into your inbox by tomorrow morning.

-Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finexanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing post-call: latency & peak QPS follow-ups

Rafael / team — quick note on batching & KV cache:
- For chat-heavy workloads with streaming, continuous small batches reduce latency but increase GPU cycles. We should model both per-token continuous serving and a hybrid where small prefix caching handles repeated context.
- If FinEx can expose session affinity (sticky routing) we'll avoid KV eviction and reduce peak costs.

I can add a short section in the sizing doc showing delta in tokens/sec and cost between sticky vs no-sticky routing. Rafael — happy to pair on the sim run after you generate the initial numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finexanalytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing post-call: latency & peak QPS follow-ups

Thanks all — confirming: payloads included are raw text (not pre-tokenized). Peak is single-region (us-west) for the next quarter. Session affinity is feasible on our side; we can add a header to preserve sticky routing.

Look forward to the sizing options. If you can include expected token/sec and estimated tokens per second per GPU (and cost estimate), that will help us plan procurement.

-Amelia
